_description: Initial Access Broker (IAB) activity - sales of corporate access (VPN, RDP, AD, webshells), enterprise stealer logs, and high-value account compromises. Uses multi-signal lookahead regex to require BOTH an access-type term AND either a sale/contact signal or a corporate-context signal (industry, revenue, geography).

rules._description: Listings selling network access to a corporate environment. Two-signal lookahead: access-type term (VPN/RDP/Citrix/Fortinet/etc.) + transaction term (selling/for sale/escrow/contact/price). The geography/industry/revenue context is what distinguishes a real IAB listing from generic discussion.
rules._fp_risk: Medium. Sysadmin and IT-support channels discuss VPN/RDP daily. Excludes catch help-desk and product-support framing. If you ingest IT-ops channels heavily, consider disabling and using only the IAB-corporate-context rule below.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - direct sale of corporate network access is among the highest-value TI signals.
rules.name: IAB - corporate access listing

rules._description: IAB listings with explicit victim characterization - industry vertical + revenue + geography. Real IAB listings almost always include 'US-based manufacturing company, revenue $X' style metadata to attract buyers. This rule fires when those characterizers appear together with access terms.
rules._fp_risk: Low. Combination of industry vertical + revenue figure + access term rarely occurs outside actual listings. May occasionally catch business-news posts about breach victims - excludes pin obvious news framing.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - victim characterization typically only appears in active listings.
rules.name: IAB - victim characterization (industry + revenue + access)

rules._description: Stealer logs targeted at corporate use - fresh credentials/cookies/sessions from infostealers, sorted for enterprise SSO targets (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, GitHub, Salesforce, AWS, GCP, Azure portal).
rules._fp_risk: Low-medium. Mature infostealer marketplaces use this language consistently. Excludes catch defensive YARA/detection content and CTF challenges.
rules._severity_rationale: High - corporate-grade stealer logs enable credential-stuffing and session-hijack attacks on enterprise SaaS.
rules.name: IAB - corporate stealer logs / cookie shop

rules._description: High-value account access - domain admin, AD compromise, cloud root/global admin sold directly. Distinguished from the general access-listing rule by elevated-privilege language. These are post-compromise listings (attacker already inside).
rules._fp_risk: Low. 'Domain admin for sale' or 'global admin compromised' is rare jargon outside underground.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - privileged access dramatically shortens the kill-chain for the buyer.
rules.name: IAB - privileged account access for sale

rules._description: Webshell, cPanel, WHM, and direct application-tier access listings. These are lower in the privilege hierarchy than network access but still actionable for buyers.
rules._fp_risk: Low-medium. Hosting-provider support channels discuss cPanel/WHM frequently - excludes pin support framing.
rules._severity_rationale: High - application-tier access is commonly the foothold for further compromise.
rules.name: IAB - webshell / panel access
